title: Remote tool contract test pollutes global import state
reasoning: The test inserts the frontend sidecar Python directory at the front of sys.path and then imports a top-level tools.registry module without restoring sys.path or cleaning sys.modules. Because this is a backend test process, that global mutation can make later tests resolve top-level imports from frontend/src/main/python first, creating order-dependent failures or masking backend import problems. The impact is concrete because the mutation is process-wide and persists after this helper returns.
recommendation: Use pytest's monkeypatch.syspath_prepend in the test, keep the import inside a scope that restores sys.path automatically, and remove any imported top-level tools modules from sys.modules after the assertion if needed. A cleaner option is to load the frontend registry by explicit file/module spec rather than globally prepending the sidecar package root.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test only verifies that the backend and frontend tool-name sets match. It does not assert that sys.path and sys.modules are restored after loading the frontend registry, so import pollution would not be caught.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test around _load_frontend_exposed_tool_names that snapshots sys.path and relevant sys.modules entries before the call, invokes the helper, and asserts no frontend path remains at sys.path[0] and no unexpected top-level tools module is left behind.
minimumFixScope: Confine the frontend registry import in tests/backend/test_remote_tool_contract.py so it does not leave process-global import state changed.
